summary: The top-N stance cards are ordered by evidence tier first and citations second, and a zero-work result reports a real apex design rather than an empty string.
reason: Citation counts are strongly age-dependent — a 2024 meta-analysis has had no time to accumulate them while a 1998 cohort study has had decades — so ordering the cards by citations alone systematically surfaced older, weaker evidence as the headline studies. Because the cut to N happens after the sort, the tier key changes WHICH works reach the cards, not merely their sequence; that is the point. Separately, Consensus() returns early for an empty corpus and so never called ApexDesign(), leaving the field at Design's zero value and emitting "apex_design": "" — a value no consumer can map to a tier. all_studies keeps fetch (relevance) order and must not be sorted; the top lists are a separate, curated view.
validated_outcome: Measured on both frozen corpora: top_refuting displaced 1 of 3 works on each, while consensus score, confidence, verdict, evidence strength and relevant count were byte-identical with the sort key on and off.
